fundamentals.name: Lumentum Holdings Inc.
fundamentals.longBusinessSummary: Lumentum Holdings Inc. manufactures and sells optical and photonic products in the Americas, the Asia-Pacific, Europe, the Middle East, and Africa. It operates through two segments, Cloud & Networking and Industrial Tech. The Cloud & Networking segment offers optical and photonic chips, components, modules, and subsystems supplied to cloud data center operators, AI/ML infrastructure providers, and network equipment manufacturer customers that are building cloud data centers and network infrastructures. Its Industrial Tech segment provides short-pulse solid-state lasers, kilowatt-class fiber lasers, diode lasers, and gas lasers that serves the semiconductor device, solar cell, display, and electric vehicle and battery manufacturing markets. The company was incorporated in 2015 and is headquartered in San Jose, California.

judgment.summary: Strong growth and profitability are overshadowed by a very high valuation and significant debt.
judgment.earningsRecap: Last quarter beat EPS estimates by 4.6%; next earnings date is 2026-08-12.
positives: Revenue growth 90.1% YoY and analyst estimates of 236.6% for current Q and 300.7% for current FY indicate explosive growth.
Operating margin of 21.8% and profit margin of 17.7% demonstrate strong profitability.
Return on equity at 22.8% shows effective use of shareholder capital.
24 analysts have a 'buy' consensus with a mean target of $1113.01, suggesting significant upside potential.
negatives: Trailing P/E of 158.44 and Forward P/E of 49.80 indicate an extremely high valuation.
PEG ratio of 0.63 suggests the stock may be undervalued relative to its growth, but this is heavily influenced by the high P/E.
Debt/Equity ratio of 111.44 and total debt nearly matching total cash suggest a leveraged balance sheet.
Free cash flow of $93.35M TTM is very low relative to market cap, indicating limited cash generation.

news.paragraph: Lumentum (LITE) has seen its stock surge recently, driven by positive analyst ratings from J.P. Morgan and a general uplift in optics stocks tied to AI demand. The company also announced a strengthened liquidity position, though its long-term growth prospects are being weighed against its high valuation. Despite a recent 4.3% jump, the stock's trajectory is being closely watched, with a significant earnings report due in August.
